coordinate_system.orientation_notes: Use the front-view frame: X horizontal, Y vertical, and Z along the cylinder axis. The horizontal cylinder axis in Section A-A corresponds to world Z; its extracted +X axis and access directions are treated as view-local. Datum A establishes the center axis but does not establish an axial zero or angular clocking.

outer cylindrical surface in free state

relationships.detail: The outer cylindrical surface is explicitly described as coaxial with datum A, established by the central bore.
The outer cylindrical surface position control references datum A.
The annular end faces terminate the cylinder normal to its bore axis. This describes geometric orientation, not an additional GD&T control.
The detailed edge breaks meet the outer cylindrical surface at both end transitions.
The detailed edge breaks meet the annular end faces at their outer rims.
The concentric annular body outlines and central section-cut reference establish the body axis as the central bore axis.

datum_scheme.datum_hierarchy_notes: A is the sole defined datum and establishes the primary bore axis. The outer-cylinder position control references A at maximum material boundary, as recorded in its applied-to text. No secondary or tertiary datum is defined; axial location and clocking are not established by this datum scheme.

assumptions.text: The explicit DETAIL X reference identifies detail_x:F1 and section_aa:F3 as the same repeated end-edge feature. detail_x:F1 is canonical because it supplies the edge-break specification and limit callouts.

Both edge observations describe the same two interchangeable end instances. They are retained as one count-two feature group, not split into individually identified ends or treated as aggregate references.

front_view:F1 describes the complete annular body rather than one particular surface. It is retained as a singleton instead of being equated with the separately extracted bore, outer cylinder, or end faces.
The front-view coordinate frame is used as the global frame. Section A-A's horizontal axial +X notation is interpreted as view-local rather than as a conflicting physical cylinder axis.
